# agent-detect

> agent-detect infers the current AI agent's harness, provider, and model — multi-harness, multi-OS,
> multi-arch — so AI agents can identify themselves accurately, as required by various AI policies
> and skills. This site is the browsable registry of its rule tables and fixture-verified results:
> which harness × provider × model combos are known, whether each is reciprocal, and the exact
> identify / trailer / explain outputs the CLI produces for them.

The detection tool itself is a prebuilt zig binary (no npm/crates package) with zero required
runtime dependencies and no network I/O at detection time:
https://github.com/bevry-vibes/agent-detect

## how the site is organised

`/` is a single-page app. Three searchable dropdowns (harness, provider, model), a free-text
search box, and the reciprocal/free toggles filter a results table; clicking a row opens that
combo's full-page results view — the from-identity results only (the site shows declared
identifications; live captures stay maintainer-side), one section per declared platform with the
plain platform name as a static pill, newest first. Each section carries the recorded outputs —
`identify`, `trailer co-author`, `trailer assisted-by`, and `explain` (plus `found`,
`check-reciprocal`, stderr lines, and meta when recorded) — with copy + copy-command buttons for
the CLI invocation behind each block. A status line reads `reciprocal · platforms · date` on a
single line. An `#index` section lists every harness, provider, and model with its canonical
alphanumeric id, its properties, and its associations (name/variation → id is the point). The
results table keeps every row in the DOM with CSS `content-visibility: auto`, so native Ctrl/Cmd+F
searches the whole list.

URL query params mirror the CLI's filters: `?harness= / ?provider= / ?model=` accept display names,
labels, and aliases and are canonicalised to the strict-slug alphanumeric ids ("Kimi Code" and
"kimi-code" land as `kimicode`); `?search=` free-text matches combo ids and dim names/ids
(substring, case-insensitive); `?email=` matches the trailer email of record; `?platform=`
(darwin/linux/windows) requires a declared fixture on that platform; `?free=`/`?reciprocal=` take
true/false. `?agent=<agent_id>` is the agent results page — a full-page replacement of the index
(not a modal); the platform param never reaches it (the page's platform pills are static). The
site header wordmark or the page's "back to results" button returns to the index with the scroll
position restored. All navigation uses the HTML5 history API
(pushState/replaceState/popstate).

## endpoints

- `/` — the app (hero, filters, results table, result pages, the #index section)
- `/index.json` — JSON results. Accepts
  `?harness=&provider=&model=&search=&agent=&email=&platform=&free=&reciprocal=` with the same
  name→id resolution on the dims. Unfiltered it returns the compact combo index; with any filter it
  embeds each matching combo's full fixtures (identify + both trailers + explain + meta), capped at
  50 combos before degrading to compact rows with `"truncated": true`.
- `/identify/<agent_id>.json` — one combo's from-identity results: every declared platform's
  fixture with its verbatim outputs and meta. agent_id is the dash-joined strict slugs, e.g.
  `cline-clinepass-deepseekv4flash`.
- `/registry.json` — the rule registry: harnesses, providers, models with policy fields (training
  postures, openness, licenses, scandal flags) and their source URLs.
- `/data/index.json` — the index file the CLI's `agent-detect index` embeds: every
  harness/provider/model with its per-entity identify fields, canonical id, variations, and
  association id arrays; `provider_map_to_free_models` (the free axis);
  `agent_map_to_platforms_reciprocal` (declared platforms + reciprocity of record per combo).
- `/data/combos.json` — the compact combo index (the same rows the table render; `free` marks the
  free-axis cells).
- `/data/agents/<agent_id>.json` — the same bytes as `/identify/<agent_id>.json`.
- `/llms.txt` — this file.

## notes for agents

- ids are strict slugs: lowercase alphanumeric with all separators stripped
  (`kimi-code` → `kimicode`, `qwen3.8-27b` → `qwen3827b`); agent_id joins the three dims with dashes
  (`cline-clinepass-deepseekv4flash`), and doubles as the trailer email local part
  (`<agent_id@local>`).
- `reciprocal: true` means the combo passes agent-detect's reciprocity requirement (per the policy
  documented in the upstream repo); `explain.state` is the detailed state
  (`reciprocal | not-reciprocal | unknown | undetectable`).
- combos listed in the registry dropdowns but absent from `/index.json` results are registry rules
  with no fixture yet — verify them live with
  `agent-detect check-reciprocal --harness=<id> --provider=<id> --model=<id>`.
- data is regenerated from the upstream repo's committed index file and from-identity channel on
  every deploy; the site stores nothing and reads nothing from visitors.
- the CLI opens this site: `agent-detect registry` prints its JSON report (`{url, query, opened}`)
  and opens with `--web` (the filters mirror the url params; all three dims or `--agent=` land on a
  combo's result page; `--no-json` prints nothing — exit status only). `agent-detect index` prints
  the rule index itself (the filters narrow all three arrays to what is available for them);
  `index --web` opens the `#index` section.
